definitions.explanation: A rhetorical device in which two lines or phrases of matching structure are set side by side, often with contrasting or paired meanings. A standard term in the study of poetry, classical Chinese verse and rhetoric.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{二行|にぎょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{対句|ついく}になっている。
examples.english: These two lines form a parallel couplet.

examples.japanese: ⟦{漢詩|かんし}→漢詩：13438_kanshi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{対句|ついく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{重|おも}んじられる→重んじる：14445_omonjiru⟧。
examples.english: Parallel couplets are highly valued in classical Chinese poetry.

examples.japanese: ⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、{対句|ついく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}った→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{効果|こうか}→効果：02726_kouka⟧⟦について→〜について：03103_nitsuite⟧⟦{学|まな}んだ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: In Japanese class, we learned about the effect of expressions that use parallelism.

notes:
A term taught in Japanese-language classes alongside other figures of speech such as {倒置法|とうちほう} (inversion) and {体言止|たいげんど}め (ending a line on a noun). A familiar example is the opening of the Heike Monogatari, whose paired lines match each other in structure.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {対句|ついく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用|もち}いる→用いる：02314_mochiiru⟧: to use parallelism
- {対句|ついく}⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧: a parallel expression
- {対句法|ついくほう}: parallelism (as a rhetorical technique)
- ⟦{律詩|りっし}→律詩：23895_risshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{対句|ついく}: the parallel couplets of a regulated verse
